system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: we have an LLM-agnostic system promptstage where we teach the planning LLM the avail-able capabilities and APIs in Incalmo. We also provide the user'senvironment specificprompt to outline attack goals
system_prompt_style.note: Environment-specific prompt rendered with attack goals/IP ranges; preprompt txt files per abstraction level shipped in repo.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: we design a queryable envi-ronment state service that maintains a structured knowledge base of the environment (akin to RAG [39]). LLMs can output high-level code that queries the service.
env_context_strategy.note: LLM issues scan/query tasks to discover environment; state service is a queryable structured DB (described as RAG-like), not snippet injection.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: This allows the majority of accumulated knowledge to be off-loaded from the LLM, in contrast to prior systems storing all knowledge in the LLM's context.
context_compaction.note: Incalmo avoids context bloat by offloading knowledge to services rather than by compacting history; no history truncation/summarizer described.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Sonnet 4 outputs tasks, Incalmo agents execute them, the agents return any results or errors, and then Sonnet 4 reacts

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: we ex-tract the Python function between the<task></task>or<query></query>tags. Then Incalmo executes the function
tool_call_format.note: LLM writes Python functions (code-as-action) delimited by XML-like task/query tags.

tool_count.evidence_quote: our abstraction for these declarative tasks follows the logical stages specified by the MITRE ATT&CK [12] and cyber kill chain [30] frame-works: scan a network, laterally move, escalate privileges, discover local information, and exfiltrate data.
tool_count.note: Five high-level declarative tasks; plus query capability. Incalmo-WHT variant exposes 19 predefined low-level tasks instead.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: we raise the level of abstraction and explicitly instruct the LLM's plan to be expressed in terms of high-level declarative tasks
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing primitive exposed to the model; low-level write_file/read_file actions exist internally for exploits but the model operates via high-level tasks.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: we teach the planning LLM the avail-able capabilities and APIs in Incalmo
tool_schema_source.note: APIs/tasks described in hand-written preprompt/codebase txt files shipped per abstraction level.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: The LLM outputs shell commands, which a second entity (e.g., human, MCP server) executes
protocol_standardization.note: MCP mentioned only as describing prior systems; Incalmo uses its own C&C API, no MCP/a2a client in the file tree.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: we explicitlydecouple planning from executionby separating Incalmo into an LLM-assisted planning layer that decideswhattasks to perform and an execution layer that decideshowto execute tasks.
loop_primitives.note: Loop: LLM outputs tasks, agents execute, LLM reacts (react) with explicit plan/execute decoupling.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: LLMs specify and compose these declarative tasks using Python functions.
planning_granularity.note: Plan expressed as per-step task function output; no persistent plan object re-read across steps (knowledge held in state/attack-graph services).

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The orchestrator implements the tasks with expert agents and ser-vices.
multi_agent_topology.note: Planning LLM orchestrates domain-specific task agents (mostly non-LLM by default).

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: We delegate the execution of these tasks to bespoke red-team agents that use reliable best practices
delegation_mechanism.note: Work handed to per-task expert agents; default agents are non-LLM, LLM-based task agents optional (Sec 6.2).

human_in_loop.note: The run loop in run_incalmo_strategy was opened. It is while True: strategy.main() until a result arrives or TIMEOUT_SECONDS (75 min) passes. The loop has no confirmation, approval or human-input step, so this is an absence coded under rule 5b. The paper also describes the system as autonomous: 'Incalmo, an LLM-assisted system for autonomously red teaming multi-host networks'. The only human-in-the-loop mention is the PentestGPT baseline, not Incalmo. The excerpt shows only the start of AttackerConfig, so a config-level gate cannot be ruled out entirely. The evidence bundle gives no commit hash for this file, so the locator omits it; confidence is medium.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the environment state service maintains a structured database of Python objects that represent the environment

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The database is updated as red team agents execute tasks.
long_term_memory.note: State DB is per-run; no cross-run memory/skill library described; logs written per timestamped run only.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: We evaluate systems on MHBench by executing 5 trials with a time limit of 75 minutes per trial.
state_persistence.note: Each trial starts fresh; no resume of an interrupted run into a running agent found.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Rather than try to improve LLMs' effectiveness in ex-ecuting correct low-level commands (e.g., adding better prompts [14], [72], self-reflection [29], [14], [62])
self_verification.note: Incalmo deliberately avoids self-reflection/verification heuristics; agents return errors but no harness-enforced tests/lint/judge.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Incalmo will execute attacks until an LLM specifies a <finished>tag or reaches a time limit.
retry_policy.note: Single autonomous run per trial; no whole-task retry policy in harness.

rollback.evidence_quote: the agents return any results or errors, and then Sonnet 4 reacts and decides the subsequent task(s)
rollback.note: No undo/revert/snapshot of changes described in the run loop or actions evidence.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Incalmo will execute attacks until an LLM specifies a <finished>tag or reaches a time limit.
termination_condition.note: Also a wall-clock time limit (TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 75*60 in incalmo_runner.py) ends the run; no matching enum value for a time-based cap.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Experiments cost at most $15 of credits
cost_controls.note: Cost is reported but no cost cap/token budget/router/caching control found in evidence.

timeouts.note: Per-run 75-minute limit; per-tool command_delay/ssh ConnectTimeout=3 present but those are exploit-level ssh options, not a harness per-tool timeout.

execution_isolation.note: Attacker runs in a Docker container (docker/attacker); targets are separate containers.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote:
docker compose exec attacker /bin/bash
uv run main.py
filesystem_access.note: Agent has full access within the attacker container and executes commands on infected hosts via C&C.

network_policy.note: Network egress needed to attack multi-host targets; only a blacklist_ips config restricts targets, no egress allowlist.

permission_model.note: Blocklist of IPs (coded static_allowlist per manual); otherwise actions execute autonomously without per-call authorization. Default empty list.

tracing.evidence_quote: we log detailed information such as raw LLM conversations, attack graph states reached (from the attack graph service), tasks executed, and the events from tasks.
tracing.note: output/example_output/action_log.jsonl shows per-action structured JSONL records.

replayability.note: A replay strategy exists in state_machine strategies; environment would differ on re-run.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: MHBench, a novel multi-host attack benchmark with 40 realistic emulated networks
eval_hooks.note: MHBench is a companion benchmark (separate OpenStack/Ansible setup); repo has a remote MHBench integration mode but the eval runner is not shown as a built-in hook in the pinned files.

guardrails.note: Blacklist of IPs restricts which hosts actions may target; no input/output filters found.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Incalmo is an autonomous AI-driven network penetration testing tool that automatically conducts intelligent red-teaming activities
target_domain.note: Domain is cyber-offense / multi-host network red teaming (penetration testing); not swe/web/gui.

model_agnostic.note: README lists OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek via LangChain registry.
